title: Hybrid content-signature cache with tiered TTLs and hot-prefix prefetch for embedding reranks
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Reduce redundant embedding computation for reranking by combining a compact content-signature (exact + proximity hashing) with a tiered cache and conservative invalidation. This ticket implements a hybrid dedupe strategy (exact content hash + fuzzy similarity signature) plus a three-tier cache: hot in-memory per-inference-node, regional Redis warm store, and cold persistent vector store. Key goals: (1) lower 95th/99th latency on rerank endpoints for common duplicate prefixes; (2) reduce global embedding qps for identical/near-identical inputs; (3) keep cache correctness during model refreshes and content drift.

Background: Current prefix-based caching is brittle across tenant normalization and model upgrades and doesn't detect near-duplicates caused by minor formatting/noise. We must detect semantic near-duplicates without over-aggressively collapsing distinct inputs (risk of stale or low-quality rerank results).

Proposed approach: 1) Compute two compact signatures at embedding ingest time: an exact salted 128-bit Murmur3-like hash (tenant salt + normalized content) and a 256-bit locality-preserving sketch (MinHash + simhash fused) used for approximate dedupe. 2) Normalize input by stable rules (strip punctuation when configured, collapse whitespace, canonicalize URLs) with per-tenant normalization flags. 3) Store cache entries keyed by exact hash (fast lookup) and maintain a small proximity index (LSH buckets) that points to candidate exact hashes for near-duplicate lookup. 4) Cache tiers and TTLs: hot (node-RAM) TTL=30s default with frequency-based pinning; warm (regional Redis) TTL sliding window 1h with decay; cold (S3-backed vector store) TTL 7d for eviction but retrievable. 5) Invalidation: model-version fingerprint included in signature metadata; on model update, we perform rolling invalidation for entries whose model fingerprint changed or mark them stale and proactively refresh-on-read. 6) Prefetch: hot-prefix detector identifies high-probability prefixes and proactively populates node-RAM from Redis with rate limits to avoid thundering herds. 7) Safety: similarity threshold calibrated to target <=0.2% false-positive semantic collisions; fallback path recomputes embedding when confidence is low or if downstream quality tests fail.

Success metrics: cache hit rate for rerank embedding requests >=20% on hotprefix traffic; reduce embedding compute qps by >=18% for tested workloads; 95th-percentile end-to-end rerank latency improvement >=25ms for routes with observed duplication.
acceptance_criteria: Automated end-to-end test shows cache hit correctly returns same rerank vector within quality tolerance for 99.7% exact matches
Benchmarked 50QPS synthetic workload with 30% duplicate inputs shows >=18% reduction in embedding compute QPS
95th-percentile rerank path latency reduced by >=25ms on hotprefix traffic during A/B rollout
Model upgrade workflow invalidates or marks stale entries and does not serve stale embeddings beyond configured TTL
Security review signed off on tenant-salting design and no plaintext tenant identifiers stored in the shared proximity index
notes: Trade-offs: fuzzy dedupe increases risk of false positives — mitigated by conservative threshold + sample-based quality checks and TTLs
Decision: use tenant-salted exact hash to prevent cross-tenant collisions and to allow aggressive eviction per-tenant
We will not attempt global LRU across tenants to avoid privacy/leakage and complexity; frequency counters are per-tenant/cohort
Prefetch strategy capped per-node to avoid bursty pulls from Redis; will add token bucket limiter in runtime loop
Storage: warm Redis entries store (hash, signature, model_fingerprint, last_seen, frequency_score) as compact protobuf, hot node cache stores raw embedding + metadata
comments: 2026-02-11 - Maya Patel: Scoped initial design with product and infra. Identified primary failure modes: false-positive dedupe and stale embeddings after model refresh. Next: prototype signatures and run synthetic dup workload.

2026-02-20 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype implemented: exact salted 128-bit hash + MinHash(64) sketches. Initial microbench: exact-hit lookup ~0.3ms, LSH candidate expansion adds 1.2ms median. Memory: per-node hot cache budget 256MB for embeddings shard.
2026-02-24 - Design review (Ana Ruiz): Recommended normalization rules list and per-tenant opt-in; noted UX requirement for 'cache-control' per-request header to bypass dedupe for sensitive flows.

2026-03-01 - Security (J. Huang): Reviewed tenant-salt approach. Agreed to store tenant salt in KMS-protected vault and only use derived per-node ephemeral salt for runtime hashing. Requested design doc update with threat model.

2026-03-05 - Perf bench: Ran 3 workload profiles (QA-synthetic, ecom-search, helpdesk). Hotprefix hit rate varied: 12% -> 27% depending on traffic skew. Observed overall ~15% embedding qps reduction on mixed traffic; Hotprefix prefetch shows 10-12ms improvement for local hits.

2026-03-09 - PR feedback (ENG): PR #7142 added proximity index using Redis-TS LSH buckets. Reviewers asked to add circuit-breaker when Redis latency spikes. Working on adding fallback path that degrades to exact-hash-only dedupe + recompute-on-miss.

2026-03-12 - Product (R. Singh): Approved A/B plan: 5% traffic ramp to start with monitoring. Agreed on metrics dashboard and rollback criteria (increase in rerank regression rate >0.5% or latency regression >10ms).
Next steps: finish Redis circuit-breaker, add model-fingerprint invalidation handler, and create A/B dashboards. Schedule rollout for 2026-03-20 if metrics pass internal canary.
